answer: Each identity claims one mesa rim segment, locks 70 credits, and posts the talus volume fallen into the canyon below. Scale is fixed by counting walnut crowns in its photo; an auditor recomputes the volume from its lidar table. Outside tolerance, a reused key, or two segments per identity burns the bond. First fee is 29; the kth pays 29+7(k-1), so the 1000th pays 7022 and 1000 fakes pay 3,525,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-photo ring fails because its walnut pattern and lidar profile are unique, so copies mismatch. Honest claimants pay 29 once, bond back after a clean recompute.
